about: Hand-authored contract for the categorical choice parser (judicial.parse_choice and Judicial.parseChoice). Every expected value was written by hand from the rules, never read back from either engine. Rules, in order: a valid JSON object with the answer key; the answer key read tolerantly when the object does not parse (the last readable key wins); the whole reply equal to an option; then, only when the reply was not cut off, an explicit answer marker (the word 'answer' followed by ':' or 'is', Markdown emphasis ignored; the last marker that names an option wins); an option at the very start followed by punctuation; and first mention last. A single-letter option counts in running text only as its capital letter, so the article 'a' is never option A. 'knownLimit' cases are still read wrongly and are kept so that a change to them is deliberate. Read by Server/tests/test_judicial.py and Tests/ExperimentKitTests/JudicialTests.swift.

cases.name: article before the stated letter
cases.text: As a doctor, I would choose B.
cases.why: The lower-case article 'a' is never option A, and the capital A of 'As' is inside a word.

cases.name: article before an answer phrase
cases.text: This is a hard case; my answer is B.
cases.why: 'my answer is' is an answer marker.

cases.name: article after the stated letter
cases.text: I choose B. It saves a life.
cases.why: First mention: B is the first capital letter that stands alone.

cases.name: bare letter
cases.text: B
cases.why: The whole reply is an option.

cases.name: lower-case letter as the whole reply
cases.text: b
cases.why: A whole-reply match ignores case: nothing else in the reply could be the article.

cases.name: letter and full stop as the whole reply
cases.text: B.
cases.why: A whole-reply match ignores a trailing full stop.

cases.name: letter then a reason
cases.text: B. Because a single death is better than five.
cases.why: An option at the very start, followed by a full stop.

cases.name: lower-case letter then a bracket and a reason
cases.text: b) Because a single death is better than five.
cases.why: At the very start, a letter followed by punctuation is an answer in either case; the article is always followed by a word.

cases.name: bold letter at the start
cases.text: **B** - pulling the lever saves a net four lives.
cases.why: Markdown emphasis around the opening letter is ignored.

cases.name: article earlier in the sentence
cases.text: In a case like this, a doctor should choose B.
cases.why: The lower-case article is never option A.

cases.name: plain final-answer line
cases.text: Final answer: B
cases.why: Answer marker.

cases.name: final-answer label in bold
cases.text: **Final answer:** B
cases.why: Markdown emphasis around the marker is ignored.

cases.name: final-answer label in bold, colon outside
cases.text: **Final answer**: B
cases.why: Markdown emphasis between the marker word and its colon is ignored.

cases.name: final-answer label in italics
cases.text: *Final answer:* B
cases.why: Markdown emphasis around the marker is ignored.

cases.name: final-answer label in underscore italics
cases.text: _Final answer:_ B
cases.why: Underscore emphasis is ignored too.

cases.name: letter in bold after the marker
cases.text: Final answer: **B**
cases.why: Markdown emphasis around the letter is ignored.

cases.name: final answer on its own last line after an argument naming both
cases.text:
Option A pulls the lever and saves five; option B refuses to kill anyone. A doctor's first duty is not to harm.
Final answer: B
cases.why: The marker outranks first mention, which would read the A named first.

cases.name: answer label
cases.text: Answer: A
cases.why: Answer marker.

cases.name: my answer is
cases.text: My answer is B
cases.why: Answer marker.

cases.name: the last marker wins
cases.text:
Answer: A. On reflection, that sacrifices a person as a means.
Final answer: B
cases.why: Several markers: the last one that names an option wins.

cases.name: a marker that names no option is passed over
cases.text: The answer is not obvious. I choose B.
cases.why: 'The answer is not' names no option, so the next rule reads the reply.

cases.name: article right after a marker
cases.text: The answer is a matter of duty, so I choose B.
cases.why: A lower-case letter after a marker counts only when punctuation or the end of the reply follows it; 'a matter' is the article.

cases.name: lower-case letter ending the reply after a marker
cases.text: Final answer: b
cases.why: A lower-case letter at the end of the reply, after a marker, is the answer.

cases.name: option word after the marker
cases.text: Having weighed both, the answer is option B.
cases.why: The word 'option' between the marker and the letter is skipped.

cases.name: names both letters while deliberating, then concludes
cases.text: A saves five but requires killing one; B lets five die without anyone acting. After weighing both, my answer is B.
cases.why: The concluding marker outranks the letters named while deliberating.

cases.name: a reply that never answers
cases.text: Both choices carry a real moral cost, and I do not think there is a right answer here.
cases.why: No option is named; a parse failure is recorded, never a guess.

cases.name: truncated argument
cases.text: Option A saves five lives at the cost of one, while option B lets five die. Weighing a doctor's duty against
cases.why: A reply cut off by the token limit never falls back to first mention.

cases.name: truncated after a final-answer line
cases.text: Option A saves five; option B saves one. Final answer: B, because a
cases.why: A truncated reply is read only through a JSON answer, the answer key, or a whole-reply match; markers are not read in it.

cases.name: truncated whole-reply match still counts
cases.text: B
cases.why: A whole-reply match is a decision even when the limit was reached.

cases.name: JSON answer
cases.text: {"answer": "B", "reasons": "Pulling the lever saves a net four lives."}
cases.why: A valid JSON object with the answer key.

cases.name: JSON answer in a fence
cases.text:
Here is my answer.
```json
{"answer": "B"}
```
cases.why: A fenced JSON object with the answer key.

cases.name: invalid JSON in a fence: unescaped quotes inside the reasons
cases.why: The object does not parse, so the answer key is read tolerantly; first mention would have read the article 'a'.

cases.name: invalid JSON: answer key before the reasons
cases.text: {"answer": "B", "reasons": "The so-called "greater good" argument treats a person as a number."}
cases.why: The answer key is read tolerantly wherever it sits.

cases.name: invalid JSON: an odd number of inner quotes
cases.text: {"answer": "B", "reasons": "The 5" figure hides a person behind a number."}
cases.why: An odd quote count makes the object look unclosed; the complete answer key is still read.

cases.name: invalid JSON: raw newlines and a tab inside the reasons
cases.text:
{"reasons": "Pulling the lever kills a person.
Doing nothing lets five die.	It is a hard case.", "answer": "B"}
cases.why: Raw control characters make the object invalid; the answer key is read tolerantly.

cases.name: invalid JSON: answer key after the reasons
cases.text: {"reasons": "A doctor must not sacrifice a "healthy" patient.", "answer": "B"}
cases.why: The answer key is found wherever it sits in the object.

cases.name: invalid JSON: the last answer key wins
cases.text:
```json
{"answer": "A", "reasons": "a "first" try"}
```
Correction:
```json
{"answer": "B", "reasons": "a "second" try"}
```
cases.why: Several readable answer keys: the last one that names an option wins.

cases.name: invalid JSON: answer key that names no option
cases.text: {"answer": "maybe", "reasons": "it is a "hard" case"}
cases.why: The key names no option and nothing else in the reply does either.

cases.name: invalid JSON with a declared key
cases.text: {"choice": "B", "why": "a "lesser" harm"}
cases.why: The study's declared key is read, not only 'answer'.

cases.name: truncated object cut before the answer key, flagged
cases.text:
```json
{"reasons": "Pulling the lever is a choice to kill a person, and
cases.why: Cut off before any answer: a failure, never the article 'a'.

cases.name: truncated object cut before the answer key, unflagged
cases.text:
```json
{"reasons": "Pulling the lever is a choice to kill a person, and
cases.why: An object opened and never closed reads as truncated from the text alone.

cases.name: truncated object after a complete answer key
cases.text: {"answer": "B", "reasons": "Pulling the lever is a choice to kill a
cases.why: The complete answer key and value were written before the cut.

cases.name: lower-case options: capital letter in prose
cases.text: I choose B.
cases.why: A single-letter option is found in running text as its capital letter, and the declared option is returned.

cases.name: lower-case options: lower-case letter after a marker
cases.text: Final answer: a
cases.why: After a marker, a lower-case letter at the end of the reply counts.

cases.name: digit options after a marker
cases.text:
Option 1 saves five; option 2 saves one.
Final answer: 2
cases.why: Digits are matched exactly.

cases.name: positions count characters, not storage units
cases.text: 😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀😀 neither B.
cases.why: Ten emoji, then 'neither' (character 11) before B (character 19). An engine that counted UTF-16 units for one option and characters for the other would put B first.

cases.name: multi-word: whole reply
cases.text: Rule for the plaintiff.
cases.why: Whole-reply match, any case. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: JSON answer
cases.text: {"answer": "rule for the defendant"}
cases.why: JSON answer. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: first mention in prose
cases.text: I would rule for the defendant, although rule for the plaintiff was argued.
cases.why: First mention, matched ignoring case. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: first mention in capitals
cases.text: Having weighed it, RULE FOR THE PLAINTIFF is my ruling.
cases.why: First mention ignores case. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: article in the reply
cases.text: This is a close case, but I would rule for the plaintiff.
cases.why: Articles never matter to multi-word options. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: option at the start
cases.text: Rule for the defendant: the contract was void.
cases.why: Start of the reply. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: truncated deliberation
cases.text: Rule for the plaintiff would honor the contract, while rule for the defendant would
cases.why: Truncated: no first mention. Unchanged.

cases.name: multi-word: a marker outranks first mention
cases.text: Counsel urged us to rule for the plaintiff. Final answer: rule for the defendant
cases.why: Changed: before this rule, first mention read the plaintiff option that counsel urged.

cases.name: known limit: a capitalised article opens the reply
cases.text: A hard case, but I choose B.
cases.why: A capital 'A' that opens a sentence cannot be told from option A without understanding the sentence. Ask for 'Final answer:' or JSON.

cases.name: known limit: the options restated as a list first
cases.text: A) Pull the lever. B) Do nothing. I would do nothing: B.
cases.why: A reply that restates the options before answering, with no marker, is read as the first option. Ask for 'Final answer:' or JSON.

cases.name: known limit: deliberates and concludes without a marker
cases.text: A saves five but requires killing one; B lets five die. I would not kill, so B.
cases.why: Without a marker, first mention reads the first letter named. Ask for 'Final answer:' or JSON.
